detection.quote: Where appropriate, a viva voce (oral) examination may be used as part of an academic misconduct investigation.

process.quote: The Tutor or Supervisor should invite the student to an informal meeting.
refer the case to a Panel Hearing for determination at Level 3.
Allegations of misconduct will normally be investigated by a designated Disciplinary Officer or their formally nominated delegate.
Students may submit a written statement and supporting evidence in advance of or following an investigation meeting.
Panel Hearings will ordinarily be conducted as remote proceedings via secure video conferencing.

If a student fails without adequate reason to attend any meeting held under this Procedure, the Chair of the Panel or Disciplinary Officer may proceed with the hearing or meeting in the student’s absence or, at their discretion, postpone the start of the hearing or meeting.
A student is entitled to have a supporter present at any stage of the disciplinary procedures outlined in this Procedure.
A student may request an appeal against the following decisions made under this Procedure:
the University aims to complete the disciplinary procedure within 90 days of an allegation being received by the University, although this may need to be extended on a case-by-case basis.
The standard of proof required for all decisions taken under this Procedure is the balance of probabilities.
Records of disciplinary proceedings will normally be held for a period of 6 years after the last action, in line with the University’s Record Retention Schedule.

outcomes.quote: Students who are found to have demonstrated poor academic practice will generally be provided with appropriate advice and guidance.

outcomes.quote: Give the student a verbal warning about their future behaviour; or
Require the student to remedy the elements of the work that were produced through misconduct and then resubmit for a capped or uncapped mark;

outcomes.quote: Where a student who has already been awarded is found to have committed academic misconduct, the award will normally be rescinded by Senate and a sanction will be applied in accordance with the below scheme.

outcomes.quote: The number of previous offences relates to offences that have received separate consideration under this Procedure.

outcomes.quote: In applying a sanction, the Disciplinary Officer or Panel should consider the penalties applied in previous similar cases, the impact on the student, any mitigating circumstances, admission of guilt or responsibility and the level of understanding shown, previous history of misconduct, the level of co-operation from the student, and any evidence of provocation, amongst other factors.

definitions.quote: Academic misconduct is defined as an attempt to obtain, obtaining, or assisting another person in obtaining an unfair advantage in an academic assessment.
Plagiarism: presenting another person’s published or unpublished work in any quantity without adequately identifying it and citing its source;
Duplication: resubmitting work in any quantity without acknowledgement or without adequate redevelopment to make it novel and appropriate to the assessment
Falsification: inventing or altering facts, data, quotations or references without acknowledgement;
Collusion: assisting another student, or being assisted by another person, in gaining an unfair advantage in an academic assessment;
Cheating: engaging in conduct that sets out to undermine the security, integrity or fairness of an assessment;
Contract cheating: contracting with another individual or body to receive or provide work in exchange for compensation of any kind, including payment.

Improper use of AI: Students shall not claim work or ideas that have been generated through Artificial Intelligence as their own; where AI usage is permitted under the guidelines of the relevant assessment, its usage must be fully cited in accordance with academic best practice on referencing.
Academic misconduct may be distinguished from poor academic practice, which is the result of inexperience or a lack of knowledge.
